project.title: Protease Regulation by Subtrate O-Glycosylation
project.projectDescription: In this study, we systematically assessed the fine-tuning of limited proteolysis in the extracellular space by glycosylation, one of the most widely observed PTMs, using cells, and applying the Terminal Amine Labeling of Substrates (TAILS) approach, a quantitative proteomics workflow for the system-wide assessment of protein N termini and protease cleavage events in complex biological samples. In addtion, we complement the study with DIA analysis, PRM and glycoproteomics analysis for further validation of the initial observations.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein samples from wt and COSMC ko MDA-MB-231 secretomes in 4M GuHCl, 250 mM HEPES pH 7.8 were reduced with 10 mM TCEP and alkylated with 40 mM CAA for 10 minutes at 95°C. Next, the samples were digested with trypsin at a 1:20 enzyme-to-protein ratio (w/w) for 16 hours at 37°C. After quenching the digestion, the samples were prepared for analysis by loading onto Evotips according to the manufacturer's instructions. The samples were analyzed on an Orbitrap Exploris™ 480 mass spectrometer, coupled with an LC Evosep One system.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files were processed using Spectronaut v.17, using DirectDIA (Deep) mode, querying against the human UniProt database (taxonomy ID: 9606, release October 2017) using modified BGS factory settings. For database search, the following parameters were used: trypsin for enzyme specificity, allowing two missed cleavages; carbamidomethyl(C) as fixed modification, and acetyl (Protein N-term) and oxidation (M), were set as variable modifications. The quantification level was set to MS1 using only proteotypic peptides. Missing values were imputed using the background signal.
